newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Syria attacks Mideast economic summit.
newsitem.headline: Syria attacks Mideast economic summit.

text.p: Syria's Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam attacked plans for a Middle East economic summit because of the impasse in the Arab-Israeli peace process, the Kuwait News Ageny reported on Monday.

"Khaddam said...the attempt to hold the Middle East-North Africa (MENA) economic summit aims at violating Arab resolutions regarding the peace process in the region," the agency said. "Violating Arab resolutions...by dealing with Israel would cause grave harm to the Arab nation."
Khaddam, accompanied by Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara, paid a short visit to the Gulf Arab state on Monday.

On Sunday Shara handed a message from Syrian President Hafez al-Assad to Qatar's Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani asking that he postpone the summit planned for November, the agency quoted "well-informed" Syrian sources as saying.
Khaddam, who left Kuwait to continue a tour of Arab states after visiting Saudi Arabia, said he would tackle "the danger of the Turkish-Israeli alliance."
"This situation requires Arab leaders to consult about it, take it seriously and study it in a fashion that would protect Arab interests."
Syria wants Turkey to understand "its interests lie in dealing with Arab and Islamic countries and not Israel," he added.
